problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$

| $v=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{20-16}[\begin{aligned}5 & 8 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}5 & 8 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}5 & 8 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
